coord_notes.shape: \(W=(I-\Pi_U)W_0\) with \(U=\mathrm{col}\,B\): the conjugacy class of corank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors (in the monoid \(\mathrm{End}\,\mathbb R^m\)) acting on \(W_0\). For \(W_0\) of full row rank the image is a copy of \(\mathrm{Gr}(r,m)\), dimension \(r(m-r)\); it has no germ at \(\theta_0\).

HF's relu projector is pointed only at \(P=0\), where \(d\rho=0\) (\(S_1=0\)) and training cannot leave; its random init is a defect. This assumes \(W_0\) of full row rank (e.g. square attention layers). On a tall layer with \(d_{out}-\operatorname{rank}W_0\ge r\) the image does contain \(\theta_0\), at any \(B\) with \(\mathrm{col}\,B\perp\mathrm{col}\,W_0\). There \(\dim S_1=rd_{in}<r(d_{out}-r)=d\) (Jacobian 8 against 16 at \((10,4,2)\)), a deficient pointing the method does not use.

coord_notes.rebasing: Re-merging composes corank-r projectors; the generated monoid consists of contractions, and each cycle can only shrink norms and ranks (a monoid, not a group).

It is DEFT restricted to \(R=0\), but only as a weak morphism, since no parameter value reproduces the frozen model.

coord_notes.rebasing: With a fixed partition and exact Cayley: idempotent up to closure (gains only the measure-zero eigenvalue \(-1\) set). HF's default Cayley-Neumann drifts (see oftv2).

methods.categorical_reading: OFT is an action-type object \(\rho(Q)=W_0\,C(Q)^\top\) whose image is an orbit of the block-orthogonal group. It can never change \(K_{\rm out}\), the spectrum or the block partial Grams (Cor II.6), however often it is re-merged. Its expressivity is that of a group orbit, regular at \(\theta_0\), with the block normaliser as covariance.

coord_notes.rebasing: Cayley-Neumann factors generate \(\prod GL^+(b)\) (\(\prod CO^+(2)\) for \(b=2\)): \(K_{\rm out}\) and the spectrum drift over merges (Thm V.3 cor. 4).

methods.categorical_reading: OFTv2 (HF's default OFTConfig) is OFT with the Cayley map replaced by its truncated Neumann series, \(R=C(Q)(I-Q^4)\). This is a quasi-orthogonal action whose image leaves the \(K_{\rm out}\) level set at order \(\|Q\|^4\) and whose rebasing closure is \(\prod GL^+(b)\) rather than \(\prod SO(b)\). With exact Cayley it is the same object as OFT.

arrows.note: Block size b = 2 only: a 2x2 Cayley-Neumann block is a scaled rotation in CO^+(2), i.e. a quasi-Givens block of qGOFT's first layer.

obstructions.reason: Cayley-Neumann images are not orthogonal (R^T R = (I - Q^4)^2), so they change K_out; near theta_0 the images of OFT and OFTv2 meet only at theta_0.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived. For b = 2, C(Q)(I - Q^4) = (1 - t^2)[[1-t^2, -2t],[2t, 1-t^2]], so the qGOFT arrow holds exactly. R^T R = (I - Q^4)^2 gives the OFT obstruction. The generated group is prod GL^+(b) (CO^+(2) at b=2) because the symmetric part has non-zero trace and traceless parts. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: The forward map \(W_{hi}+U_{lo}\Sigma_{lo}V_{lo}^\top\) is a reparametrisation; the projected gradients are optimizer data (a backward compression \(c_t\)).
coord_notes.shape: With \(U_{lo}\perp U_{hi}\), \(V_{lo}\perp V_{hi}\) enforced and \(k=\min(m,n)-e\), the image is \(\theta_0+\{U_\perp ZV_\perp^\top\}\), a linear block of dimension \((m-e)(n-e)\) in the SVD frame (rank \(\le k\) is automatic). This holds for SGD-type rules; Adam's elementwise preconditioner leaves the projected subspace, and the object is then the split cone \(W_{hi}+\mathcal M_{\le k}\) (Cone*).
coord_notes.base_point: Initialised at \(W_0\)'s own SVD with \(\Sigma_{lo}\) invertible: regular.
coord_notes.gauge: \(U\Sigma V^\top\) with a trainable diagonal \(\Sigma\): the generic fibre has dimension \(k^2+k\); only the torus \((D_1,D_1^{-1}\Sigma D_2^{-1},D_2)\) acts linearly, the rest is absorption of \(\Sigma\), as in AdaLoRA's \(P\Lambda Q\).
coord_notes.covariance: SVD frame of \(W_0\): \(CO\times CO\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Frames are frozen within a task, so idempotent; the continual-learning protocol recomputes the SVD per task and shrinks the trainable block (a schedule across tasks).

methods.categorical_reading: OSF is a split (MiLoRA-type) pointing of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_k\) with \(k\) half the rank, plus a backward projection that confines the factors to the complements of the frozen top singular subspaces. Under that projection its reach is the linear minor block \(\theta_0+U_\perp(\cdot)V_\perp^\top\) of the SVD frame, the exact dual of PSOFT, which adapts only inside the principal block.

A single run stays far from the orbit; rebasing walks all of it because the plane graph is connected.

Coordinate 'group' kept.

methods.categorical_reading: ETHER is an unpointed action-type object: its image is a compact set of block reflections \(W_0H^B\subset W_0\cdot O(n)\) at fixed distance from \(\theta_0\). It preserves \(K_{\rm out}\) and the spectrum (Cor II.6) but has no base point over \(\theta_0\); its 'bounded deviation' is literally \(\|H_j-I\|_F=2\).

obstructions.reason: ETHER is unpointed: for an even number n of blocks its image lies in Im HRA_n (n reflections with disjoint supports), but only through a weak morphism, never a pointed one.
Reflections have eigenvalue -1, which the Cayley map never produces.

Its default pointing (\(v=-u\)) is the vertex of the cone of such perturbations, so unlike ETHER it is pointed, but it sits at an apex, like zero-init LoRA. Its update has rank \(\le2\) per block and side, so LoRA of that rank simulates it.
